{"parentUuid":"951a8277-abbf-4225-9824-590792707bd3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e08452c1-f689-4079-9549-4a0322d2a6dc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EgtZqBBwHVbhAxVAgqaDPo","type":"tool_result","content":"===== SPEC\ntitle:\tSpec: Document-style authoring — Editor, tables, Charts, Site preview\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\nlabels:\tspec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t14\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. A new ref is checked, in the same transaction as the insert, against **both** tables' live refs and `deleted_refs`. On the (extremely unlikely) collision, a fresh ref is generated and the insert retried, and it fails loudly after 3 attempts.\n  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.\n  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.\n  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.\n  - **Attribute values:**\n    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.\n    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.\n    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.\n    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.\n  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.\n  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n- **Round trip:**\n  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n  - The Editor HTML for a body with locked blocks contains their tokens and their sanitized rendered HTML, and none of their raw Markdown bytes anywhere in the response.\n  - A save with an unknown locked token, a duplicated token, or a forged token that carries its own content is refused. The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- #15 T12: Site preview\n- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- #20 T17: Chart builder\n- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"5a385e87-1840-49fa-ba47-3acf62b01743","timestamp":"2026-09-30T22:52:42.708Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"===== SPEC\ntitle:\tSpec: Document-style authoring — Editor, tables, Charts, Site preview\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\nlabels:\tspec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t14\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. A new ref is checked, in the same transaction as the insert, against **both** tables' live refs and `deleted_refs`. On the (extremely unlikely) collision, a fresh ref is generated and the insert retried, and it fails loudly after 3 attempts.\n  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. The test collects every element name and every attribute name and asserts both sets are subsets of the fixed vocabulary. It asserts every `fill`/`stroke` is a palette constant, every `class` is a fixed name, and every `id` matches `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, with no `href`, `style`, or `on*` anywhere.\n  - Hostile writer strings (`<script>`, `\"><svg onload=…>`, `javascript:`, `</title>`, `&`) in every text field appear only as escaped text content, which the same parse confirms.\n  - Placeholders: a writer who types the placeholder shape into the body gets it rendered as inert text. Two charts get distinct placeholders.\n  - An invalid block reaching render outputs only the fixed \"could not be shown\" text.\n  - Bar charts have a zero baseline. \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation. The privacy note appears exactly once.\n- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. A draft Report appears in its own preview's nav but not in any other page or preview. Nothing is saved. Login and CSRF are required.\n- **Draft leak and export:** T08's crawl test still passes, with no draft content in `site/`, and the export is still identical to the live site.\n- **Browser behaviour** (toolbar, paste, the table controls, the chart dialog, the unsaved-changes warning) is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari. These checks add to the pytest suite and never replace it. Each ticket's closing comment records, for each check:\n  - the browser and exact version\n  - the viewport size\n  - the actions performed, step by step\n  - the observed result, with pass or fail\n  - the screenshots as supporting evidence\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Pie, stacked, scatter, and dual-axis charts. Chart colour choice.\n- Autosave, revision history, and collaborative editing.\n- Uploading a pasted or dropped picture (it's refused, with a pointer to \"Insert image\").\n- A Markdown source toggle for writers.\n- Underline, fonts, colours, text alignment, code blocks, horizontal rules.\n- Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI), which is ADR-004 unchanged.\n- Site preview of list pages (home, Data Bites index). The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- #15 T12: Site preview\n- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- #20 T17: Chart builder\n- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"e413f8bb-d478-4568-8446-a5b11b0afbca","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":5},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"951a8277-abbf-4225-9824-590792707bd3","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f9c9dd4-e223-4ae0-b659-f5d52d1a7913","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"4b8eeddc-6bbb-4d8c-a15c-30c1f2567aae","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e08452c1-f689-4079-9549-4a0322d2a6dc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KXbkmeFU9UFqx7ubTWmTnb","type":"tool_result","content":"app:\n__init__.py\n__pycache__\nauth.py\nchart_images.py\ncli.py\ncontent.py\ndata_bites.py\ndb.py\neditor.py\nflash.py\nmain.py\nmarkdown_form.py\npublic_site.py\npublish.py\nrendering.py\nreports.py\nroutes\nsettings.py\nsite_links.py\ntemplating.py\nuploads.py\nusers.py\n\nstatic:\neditor.js\n       6 app/__init__.py\n      67 app/auth.py\n     141 app/chart_images.py\n      55 app/cli.py\n     194 app/content.py\n      71 app/data_bites.py\n     105 app/db.py\n     348 app/editor.py\n      28 app/flash.py\n      74 app/main.py\n     397 app/markdown_form.py\n     324 app/public_site.py\n      40 app/publish.py\n     172 app/rendering.py\n     159 app/reports.py\n      39 app/settings.py\n     141 app/site_links.py\n      29 app/templating.py\n      90 app/uploads.py\n     113 app/users.py\n     617 static/editor.js\n    3210 total\n\"\"\"Editor HTML to Markdown in its standard form (spec #14, ADR-005).\n\nThe Editor posts HTML; the body is stored as Markdown. app.editor sanitizes\nthe posted HTML with nh3 first, and this module turns what is left into\nMarkdown, written one standard way, with stdlib `html.parser`. It writes only\nwhat the Editor supports: paragraphs, Sections (H2) and Subsections (H3),\nbulleted and numbered lists, block quotes, tables, and bold, italic, line\nbreaks, `https:`/`mailto:` and site links (app.site_links), and chart images\ninline. Any other element is let through as its text. Everything the writer typed is escaped, so it\nrenders as the text it is and never as Markdown syntax.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace\nfrom html.parser import HTMLParser\n\nfrom app.content import ContentError\nfrom app.rendering import LINK_SCHEMES\nfrom app.site_links import REFERENCE\n\n# A locked block's token (app.editor): on its own, a top-level paragraph that\n# the stored block is put back in place of. The Editor shows the block as an\n# empty <div data-locked=\"locked-<n>\">, and it is written as its token.\nLOCKED_TOKEN = re.compile(r\"locked-(\\d+)\")\n_LOCKED = \"data-locked\"\n_LOCKED_MOVED = (\"A part of the body that can't be edited here was moved into a list, \"\n                 \"quote, table, or paragraph. Move it back, or remove it.\")\n_LOCKED_FORGED = (\"A part of the body that can't be edited here was changed. Reload the \"\n                  \"page to get it back.\")\n\n# An <img>'s src -> the name of the item's chart image it shows; None for\n# any other picture, which is dropped.\nImageName = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass _Element:\n    tag: str\n    attrs: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    children: list[_Element | str] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n\n# Elements with no end tag, which never hold children.\n_VOID = {\"br\", \"img\", \"hr\", \"input\", \"meta\", \"link\", \"wbr\", \"col\", \"source\"}\n# Elements whose content is never text for the body (nh3 drops them too).\n_SKIPPED = {\"script\", \"style\", \"template\", \"head\", \"title\"}\n\n\nclass _TreeBuilder(HTMLParser):\n    \"\"\"The HTML as a tree of _Elements. Forgiving: an end tag closes the\n    nearest open element of its name, and one with none open is ignored.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)\n        self.root = _Element(\"root\")\n        self._open = [self.root]\n        self._skipping = 0\n\n    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):\n        if self._skipping or tag in _SKIPPED:\n            self._skipping += tag not in _VOID\n            return\n        element = _Element(tag, {name: value or \"\" for name, value in attrs})\n        self._open[-1].children.append(element)\n        if tag not in _VOID:\n            self._open.append(element)\n\n    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):\n        if not self._skipping and tag not in _SKIPPED:\n            self._open[-1].children.append(_Element(tag, {n: v or \"\" for n, v in attrs}))\n\n    def handle_endtag(self, tag):\n        if self._skipping:\n            self._skipping -= tag in _SKIPPED or 0\n            return\n        for depth in range(len(self._open) - 1, 0, -1):\n            if self._open[depth].tag == tag:\n                del self._open[depth:]\n                return\n\n    def handle_data(self, data):\n        if not self._skipping:\n            self._open[-1].children.append(data)\n\n\ndef _tree(html: str) -> _Element:\n    builder = _TreeBuilder()\n    builder.feed(html)\n    builder.close()\n    return builder.root\n\n\n# Every ASCII punctuation character that can start Markdown syntax anywhere in\n# a line. A backslash before any ASCII punctuation is always a literal.\n_ESCAPED = re.compile(r\"([\\\\`*_\\[\\]<>&|#~!])\")\n_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r\"[ \\t\\n\\r\\f]+\")\n# At the start of a line, the syntax that _ESCAPED leaves alone: a list\n# marker, a setext underline, or a numbered list's \"1.\" or \"1)\".\n_LINE_START = re.compile(r\"^(?:([-+=])|(\\d+)([.)]))\")\n# In a link's destination: what would end it early, and what Markdown would\n# otherwise read as an escape or an entity.\n_DESTINATION_ENCODED = re.compile(r\"[\\x00-\\x20\\x7f<>]\")\n_DESTINATION_ESCAPED = re.compile(r\"([\\\\()&])\")\n\n# A line break, in inline Markdown before it is split into lines. Writer text\n# never holds one: _escape turns every newline into a space.\n_BREAK = \"\\n\"\n_BOLD = {\"strong\", \"b\"}\n_ITALIC = {\"em\", \"i\"}\n\n# The title is the page's only H1, so a pasted H1 becomes a Section; the\n# Editor has no level below a Subsection.\n_HEADING_LEVELS = {\"h1\": 2, \"h2\": 2, \"h3\": 3, \"h4\": 3, \"h5\": 3, \"h6\": 3}\n_LISTS = {\"ul\", \"ol\"}\n_TABLE_SECTIONS = {\"thead\", \"tbody\", \"tfoot\"}\n_CELLS = {\"th\", \"td\"}\n# Elements that hold blocks, not inline text. Any other element is inline;\n# one the Editor doesn't write (a <div> or <section> from a paste) is a\n# wrapper, and only what is in it is kept.\n_BLOCK_TAGS = {\"p\", \"blockquote\", \"table\", \"hr\", \"pre\", \"li\", \"tr\", \"caption\",\n               *_LISTS, *_HEADING_LEVELS, *_TABLE_SECTIONS, *_CELLS,\n               \"div\", \"section\", \"article\", \"header\", \"footer\", \"main\", \"aside\", \"nav\",\n               \"figure\", \"figcaption\", \"address\", \"details\", \"summary\", \"dl\", \"dt\", \"dd\",\n               \"center\"}\n_ALIGNMENTS = {\"text-align:left\": \":--\", \"text-align:right\": \"--:\",\n               \"text-align:center\": \":-:\"}\n\n\ndef is_link(href: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether the Editor keeps a link to `href` (spec #14, \"Links\"): an\n    `https:` or `mailto:` address, or a site link.\"\"\"\n    return href.lower().startswith(LINK_SCHEMES) or REFERENCE.fullmatch(href) is not None\n\n\ndef _escape(text: str) -> str:\n    return _ESCAPED.sub(r\"\\\\\\1\", _WHITESPACE.sub(\" \", text))\n\n\ndef _escape_line_start(line: str) -> str:\n    return _LINE_START.sub(lambda m: f\"\\\\{m[1]}\" if m[1] else f\"{m[2]}\\\\{m[3]}\", line)\n\n\ndef _destination(url: str) -> str:\n    url = _DESTINATION_ENCODED.sub(lambda m: f\"%{ord(m[0]):02X}\", url)\n    return _DESTINATION_ESCAPED.sub(r\"\\\\\\1\", url)\n\n\ndef _is_block(node: _Element | str) -> bool:\n    return isinstance(node, _Element) and (node.tag in _BLOCK_TAGS or _LOCKED in node.attrs)\n\n\ndef _locked_token(node: _Element) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The token of a locked block as the Editor posts it: empty, since what\n    it shows is only for display and what is saved comes from the stored\n    body. Anything else was not made by the Editor.\"\"\"\n    token = node.attrs[_LOCKED]\n    if not LOCKED_TOKEN.fullmatch(token) or any(\n            isinstance(child, _Element) or child.strip() for child in node.children):\n        raise ContentError(_LOCKED_FORGED)\n    return token\n\n\ndef _indent(text: str, first: str, rest: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"`text` with `first` before its first line and `rest` before each\n    other non-empty line.\"\"\"\n    lines = text.split(\"\\n\")\n    return \"\\n\".join([first + lines[0], *(rest + line if line else \"\" for line in lines[1:])])\n\n\ndef _start(ol: _Element) -> int:\n    start = ol.attrs.get(\"start\", \"1\").strip()\n    return int(start) if start.isdigit() and len(start) <= 9 else 1\n\n\ndef _items(listing: _Element) -> list[list[_Element | str]]:\n    \"\"\"A list's items, each as its children. A list put straight inside a\n    list, not in an item (as some browsers indent), belongs to the item\n    before it.\"\"\"\n    items: list[list[_Element | str]] = []\n    for child in listing.children:\n        if isinstance(child, _Element) and child.tag == \"li\":\n            items.append(list(child.children))\n        elif isinstance(child, _Element) or child.strip():\n            if not items:\n                items.append([])\n            items[-1].append(child)\n    return items\n\n\ndef _rows(table: _Element) -> list[_Element]:\n    \"\"\"A table's rows, in order, from its sections or straight inside it.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for child in table.children:\n        if isinstance(child, _Element) and child.tag == \"tr\":\n            rows.append(child)\n        elif isinstance(child, _Element) and child.tag in _TABLE_SECTIONS:\n            rows.extend(row for row in child.children\n                        if isinstance(row, _Element) and row.tag == \"tr\")\n    return rows\n\n\ndef _without_breaks(node: _Element | str) -> _Element | str:\n    \"\"\"A table cell's content with each line break as a space: a Markdown\n    table row is one line.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(node, str):\n        return node\n    if node.tag == \"br\":\n        return \" \"\n    return _Element(node.tag, node.attrs, [_without_breaks(child) for child in node.children])\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass _Converter:\n    image_name: ImageName | None\n    # Off in a table cell, where a line never starts a block.\n    escape_line_starts: bool = True\n\n    # Inline.\n\n    def inline(self, node: _Element | str, marks: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> str:\n        \"\"\"One node's inline Markdown. `marks` are what is already open\n        around it (\"bold\", \"italic\", \"link\"), so none is written twice.\"\"\"\n        if isinstance(node, str):\n            return _escape(node)\n        if _LOCKED in node.attrs:\n            raise ContentError(_LOCKED_MOVED)\n        if node.tag == \"br\":\n            return _BREAK\n        if node.tag == \"img\":\n            return self.image(node)\n        if node.tag in _BOLD:\n            return self.delimit(\"**\", node, marks, \"bold\")\n        if node.tag in _ITALIC:\n            return self.delimit(\"*\", node, marks, \"italic\")\n        if node.tag == \"a\":\n            return self.link(node, marks)\n        return self.content(node, marks)\n\n    def content(self, node: _Element, marks: frozenset[str]) -> str:\n        return \"\".join(self.inline(child, marks) for child in node.children)\n\n    def delimit(self, marker: str, node: _Element, marks: frozenset[str], mark: str) -> str:\n        content = self.content(node, marks | {mark})\n        core = content.strip(\" \")\n        if mark in marks or not core:\n            return content\n        # Markdown only opens and closes emphasis next to non-space characters.\n        lead = content[:len(content) - len(content.lstrip(\" \"))]\n        trail = content[len(content.rstrip(\" \")):]\n        return f\"{lead}{marker}{core}{marker}{trail}\"\n\n    def link(self, node: _Element, marks: frozenset[str]) -> str:\n        text = self.content(node, marks | {\"link\"})\n        href = node.attrs.get(\"href\", \"\").strip()\n        if \"link\" in marks or not text.strip() or not is_link(href):\n            return text\n        return f\"[{text}]({_destination(href)})\"\n\n    def image(self, node: _Element) -> str:\n        name = self.image_name(node.attrs.get(\"src\", \"\")) if self.image_name else None\n        if name is None:\n            return \"\"\n        return f\"![{_escape(node.attrs.get('alt', ''))}]({_destination('image:' + name)})\"\n\n    def lines(self, nodes: list[_Element | str]) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"Inline nodes as lines of Markdown, split at line breaks, with no\n        empty line at either end.\"\"\"\n        lines = [line.strip(\" \")\n                 for line in \"\".join(self.inline(node) for node in nodes).split(_BREAK)]\n        if self.escape_line_starts:\n            lines = list(map(_escape_line_start, lines))\n        while lines and not lines[-1]:\n            lines.pop()\n        while lines and not lines[0]:\n            lines.pop(0)\n        return lines\n\n    # Blocks.\n\n    def blocks(self, element: _Element, *, top: bool = False) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"An element's children as Markdown blocks, in order. A run of\n        inline children between blocks is a paragraph. Only the `top`, the\n        body itself, may hold a locked block.\"\"\"\n        blocks: list[str | None] = []\n        run: list[_Element | str] = []\n        # The marker of the list just written, if the last block is a list:\n        # {"parentUuid":"fe87a3f3-eb6e-41b1-ac55-7a41740996ff","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaTtntD6LRfarL3E1jsc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The leading-`+` change and step 3 are both done and committed, and the full suite passes (669 tests).\n\n**`+` counts as a number** (`c851b14`)\n- `+3%`, `+2` and `+$1,200` now right-align their column; `+-5`, `-+5` and `(+3)` don't count.\n- I'd missed one earlier T13 test that expected the `+3%` column to be left-aligned. The full-suite run caught it and I've updated it.\n- I posted the change as an amendment on the spec issue: https://github.com/DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/14#issuecomment-5921212472\n\n**Save-path tests** (`75c1121`)\n- A Google Sheets range (styled cells, a line break inside a cell, a cell merged across the row) is stored as the expected Markdown table.\n- Bold, italic and links inside cells survive, and a `|` is escaped.\n- A table already in the standard form comes back from the Editor with exactly the same bytes.\n\nAll three passed on their first run, because T13's table code already handled these cases. To check they can fail, I broke the code twice on purpose: once so pipes weren't escaped, once so every column was left-aligned. {"parentUuid":"e203cc85-6608-4b00-827e-3c2bcf25a8c3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ffda3dd7-57b4-492c-9494-eb388b16fa11","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/skills/synced/c27537d6-7985-4b77-ad11-069d3a056783_3f882942-dfce-46fb-9f0d-f268a67a0f23/chrome-browser\n\n# Claude in Chrome\n\nClaude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.\n\nIf the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.\n\n## Loading the tools\n\nIf the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:\n\n```\nToolSearch with query \"select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp\"\n```\n\nClaude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.\n\n## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab\n\nAt the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:\n\n1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.\n2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.\n3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.\n\n## Site permissions\n\nClaude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.\n\n## Recording a GIF\n\nFor multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example \"login_process.gif\").\n\n## Reading console output\n\n`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern \"[MyApp]\" to keep only the application's own logs.\n\n## Alerts and dialogs\n\nClaude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:\n\n1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a \"Delete\" button) unless necessary.\n2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.\n3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.\n\nIf a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.\n\n## Staying on task, and when to stop\n\nClaude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:\n\n- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts\n- the extension gives no response\n- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out\n- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents\n- several approaches have not completed the task\n\nClaude does not keep retrying the same failing action.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"4ff5c1cf-739e-4542-95bd-7d76f494785d","timestamp":"2026-09-30T23:11:06.384Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01LVErrpZa54PssqkZ8VanXy","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f9c9dd4-e223-4ae0-b659-f5d52d1a7913","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

I tested the new table code in Chrome 154 on a new Data Bite and didn't save it, so nothing was written to the database.\n\n**What I checked in Chrome, and what happened:**\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n| Insert table | 3×3 table with a header row goes in after the current paragraph. The table controls appear and Insert table greys out while the cursor is in the table. |\n| Row above / Row below / Column left / Column right | Each goes in the right place, and the cursor moves into the new row or column. |\n| Remove row / Remove column | Each removes the right one; the cursor moves to the nearest remaining cell. |\n| Row above on the header row | The new row becomes the header and the old header becomes an ordinary row. |\n| Remove row on the header row | The next row becomes the header. |\n| Remove table | Leaves one empty paragraph with the cursor in it. It first left two; I fixed that. |\n| Excel clipboard HTML (simulated) | Merges split, the first row became the header, same result as the pytest test. |\n| Sheets clipboard HTML, cursor mid-paragraph (simulated) | The table goes after the paragraph, never inside it. |\n| Tab-separated text (simulated) | Becomes a table, including a quoted value with a line break in it. |\n| Paste while the cursor is in a cell | Inserts only text on one line, never a table inside a table. |\n| Site preview | Server-rendered; numeric columns right-aligned. |\n| 8-column table at a 386px viewport | Scrolls inside its own wrapper, and the table controls wrap onto two lines. Screenshots: `/var/folders/ng/p9btd2gd2nl52482qg2dd9700000gn/T/claude-chrome-screenshots-kTW0t0/screenshot-1790810025192-19.jpg` and `…-1790810041011-20.jpg` |\n| Console | No errors. |\n\n**The pastes were simulated.** I fired paste events carrying the same clipboard HTML as the pytest fixtures. That exercises `editor.js`, but it isn't a real paste from Excel or Sheets. I also can't drive Safari from here. The closing comment needs, from you, in both Chrome and Safari:\n- a real paste from Excel and from Sheets\n- one pass through the controls\n- the browser version, viewport, steps and a screenshot for each\n\n**Found along the way, not fixed:** at 386px the Data Bites list page (Updated, Publish and Unpublish columns) is wider than the screen, so the whole page scrolls sideways. It was like that before T15; it could go in the later admin design pass.\n\nThe admin console is still running at http://localhost:8000/admin (PID 26731) if you want to do the checks now. After that, the last steps are `/code-review`, posting the findings on #18, and the `Closes #18` commit. {"parentUuid":"01e2f101-b810-4b81-a179-9de5a8d3a4c1","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"0ec2379a-c389-46cb-986c-56a90e5a66fc","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since a662dcc — ticket #18 (T15: Tables in the Editor), spec #14"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"e6f282c3-a54e-40bd-99c9-b1727cda26ba","timestamp":"2026-09-30T23:25:32.027Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01Td7BAwQNUS66JGLbwzmr4v","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f9c9dd4-e223-4ae0-b659-f5d52d1a7913","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

The number regex matches the spec's rules plus the approved `+` amendment (`+-5` and `(+3)` are rejected). `_grid` and `regularTables` use the same unmerge logic. Pipes are escaped, and round trips are tested and stable.\n  \n  **(a) Missing or partial**\n  - Outstanding, as expected: \"Browser check recorded in the closing comment: paste from Excel and from Sheets, each control, and a wide table at 390px…\" This is a manual step, not a code defect.\n  - \"Tests: Excel-style HTML becomes the expected Markdown table\". The `EXCEL`/`SHEETS` tests post raw clipboard HTML straight to the server. The real path goes through the client's `cleanPasted` → `regularTables` → `buildTable` first, which strips `colspan`/`rowspan`. So the client-side unmerge and the TSV parsing have no automated test. Only the browser check covers them.\n  - \"numeric columns are right-aligned automatically\". This only happens on an Editor save. A table typed in the Markdown fallback, or an untouched stored body, keeps whatever alignment it was stored with. That follows from the approved save-time decision, but it's worth saying in the closing comment.\n  \n  **(b) Scope creep**\n  - None of substance. Two small additions: a paste into a cell is flattened to plain text, and \"Insert table\" is disabled inside a table. Both are needed to keep the spec's \"a Markdown table row is one line\" true.\n  - `N/A` is treated as missing because the check is case-insensitive. The spec only lists `n/a`. This is a harmless widening.\n  \n  **(c) Implemented but looks wrong**\n  - **Nested tables corrupt the row.** \"A pipe character in a cell is escaped\". `regularTables` handles inner tables first but leaves them inside the outer cell. On the server, `cell()` writes the inner table's own `|` characters unescaped. I probed it with `saved()`: the output was `| a | | x | y | | --: | --: | | 1 | 2 | |`, a row wider than its header. Excel and Sheets never produce this, but a paste from a web page can.\n  - **Inline formatting can split a number.** \"every non-empty cell is numeric\". `_text` joins a cell's children with spaces, so `<b>1</b>,234` reads as `1 ,234`. `<a>12</a>%` reads as `12 %`. Either one left-aligns a numeric column.\n  - **Excel's Accounting format isn't counted as a number.** \"a leading `-` or `$` … `(3.2)`\". Accounting cells copy as `$ 1,234`, `$ (3.2)` or `$ -`, all of which fail the regex. `$(1,000)` fails too, though `($1,000)` passes. This is arguably inside the spec's wording, but Accounting format is common in IR sheets.\n  - **Header rule under \"Row above\".** \"The first row is always the header row\". The rule holds, but \"Row above\" on the header row demotes the old header to a body row. Its text (e.g. \"Enrolled\") then left-aligns that column. It's consistent with the rule but likely to surprise a writer, so check it during the browser pass.\n  - **Not a problem:** `&nbsp;` blank cells and a rowspan reaching into an empty `<tr>` both behaved correctly when I probed them.\n</agent-message>"}
